messages.subject: Problem Running Report Survey
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run the report survey function but I always obtained this error:

Error: Cannot read date format in CTtable[, setupCol]. Output is all NA. expected: %Y-%m-%D actual: 2021-01-28

I think apparently the format of my dates columns are not accurate. As I had to do some changes to the data, I had to apply some changes on these columns and change the format. Here is the code I run:
reportTest <- surveyReport (recordTable          = Record_Table_PLWS_GridA,
                            CTtable              = Camera_Deployment_PLWS_GridA,
                            speciesCol           = "Species",
                            stationCol           = "Station",
                            setupCol             = "Setup_date",
                            retrievalCol         = "Retrieval_date",
                            CTDateFormat         = "%Y-%m-%D", 
                            recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTimeOriginal",
                            recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                            CTHasProblems        = FALSE)

How do I change the format of the dates column for it to work ?

Thank you for your help,

Regards,

Emeline Auda

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Problem Running Report Survey
parts:
Hi Emeline, 
this is a bit surprising, since the error message suggests that the format is ok. Can you please share the output of 
str(Camera_Deployment_PLWS_GridA)
? Maybe there some issue that I can't see right now or the error message is not correct. What changes did you apply to the data? And are you sure that the data format (e.g. order of day and month) is consistently correct?

Alternatively, you can try with the (simpler) syntax from the lubridate package:
CTDateFormat         = "ymd", 

Just be aware that you need to install the lubdridate package first. 
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Problem Running Report Survey
parts:
Hi Emeline & David, 
David is right, I didn't check carefully enough. See ?strptime:

%d
Day of the month as decimal number (01–31).

%D
Date format such as %m/%d/%y: the C99 standard says it should be that exact format (but not all OSes comply).

So it must be %d and not %D. Since all that strptime stuff can be quite confusing, I'd recommend the lubridate format. 

David, with regard to Emeline's second question, I saw the email but don't know why it doesn't appear here on the group. I answered personally via email already.
Best regards,
Jürgen
